config kernel="${KERNEL}"

# A volume is mounted at the given guest path.
vimto -volume outer:/data exec -- cat /data/file
stdout ^outer$

# Volumes are mounted in the order given, so a nested volume goes after its
# parent.
vimto -volume outer:/data -volume inner:/data/inner exec -- cat /data/file /data/inner/file
stdout ^outer$
stdout ^inner$

# The working directory is mounted last, so a volume can't hide it.
vimto -volume outer:${WORK}/.. exec -- cat outer/file
stdout ^outer$

# Sharing the same directory twice is fine.
vimto -volume outer:/data -volume outer/:/data/ exec -- cat /data/file
stdout ^outer$

# Two directories can't be mounted at the same guest path.
! vimto -volume outer:/data -volume inner:/data exec -- true
stderr 'both mounted at /data'

# The directory of a binary which is masked in the guest is shared automatically.
new-tmp
cp prog ${TMPDIR}/prog
chmod 0755 ${TMPDIR}/prog
vimto exec ${TMPDIR}/prog
stdout ^masked$

# Also when the binary is reached through a symlink.
symlink link -> ${TMPDIR}
vimto exec link/prog
stdout ^masked$

# Relative paths in the configuration are resolved against the directory
# containing the config, not the cwd.
exec git init -q
config kernel="${KERNEL}" 'volumes=[{host="outer",guest="/data"}]'
mkdir sub
cd sub
vimto exec -- cat /data/file
stdout ^outer$

# The working directory is not shared when it is the root.
cd /
vimto -kernel ${KERNEL} exec -- true

-- prog --
#!/bin/sh
echo masked
-- outer/file --
outer
-- inner/file --
inner
